note: Single source of truth for the fixed GOAL. Edit numbers here: the latency model, the reports viewer, and the converter all read this file. Durations are nanoseconds. block_count is how many block times the transaction path spans (a per-phase consensus plan). The E2E formula follows the transaction lifecycle: E2E = network_rtt_ns/2 (client request -> RPC; the submission response is off the critical path, so only half the round trip counts) + send_tx_p99_ns (in-RPC sendTransaction handler) + block_count*block_time_ns (consensus) + ingest_p99_target_ns (meta available -> ingested in RPC) + network_rtt_ns (getTransaction request + response round trip) + get_tx_p99_ns (in-RPC getTransaction handler). No slice depends on a measured client<->RPC network time: the network legs are hardcoded constants from the assumed 50 ms round trip. A phase that omits ingest_p99_target_ns has it derived from the E2E budget: e2e_budget_ns - block_count*block_time_ns - (3*network_rtt_ns/2 + send_tx_p99_ns + get_tx_p99_ns).
query_p99_note: Read-path design target, one number for every phase: no query cell (type x tier x concurrency) may exceed this p99. It sits outside fixed_estimates because it is not a slice of the E2E formula — the read benchmarks judge against it directly.
query_load_note: Open-loop query load model: per endpoint x profile x phase RPS floors on a single RPC node, derived 2026-08-27 from the management read/write patterns guideline (benchmarking hub, 856-query-load-targets.md). Load is an arrival rate, not a concurrency level: each cell is paced at ladder x floor (0.5x/1x/2x); the verdict cell is 1x. Profiles are keyed by dataset model name (the dataset name with its per-ledger tx count stripped: sac-6000 -> sac). Per-profile arrays are indexed by phase: [phase 1, phase 2, phase 3]. The p99 SLA at the target rate is query_p99_target_ns above. get_tx_in_rpc_p99_ns is getTransaction's additional in-RPC p99 target — a separate verdict from the E2E-slice estimate in fixed_estimates. events_page_budget_ns is getEvents' additional per-phase MEAN page-latency budget (a sequential subscriber needs each page's cursor, so mean overrun accumulates as lag), not a p99.
